requirement:
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
rationale:
I found no gap in the code or tests for `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`.

**Implementation**
- **Parse, resolve, hash.**
  - `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_input]` dispatches to `validate_outline_input`, which is reached from it.
  - That function checks the keys, `file`, `item` and `hash` shapes, then calls `InputSelector::resolve` (`src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[resolve]`).
  - `resolve` parses the file through `OutlineCache::parse`, which picks a profile by path and returns `cannot parse <lang> source: …` on a syntax error. It then resolves the selector through `ParsedSource::resolve`.
  - `validate_outline_input` compares `node.hash` (the node's structural hash) with the recorded hash. It reports `outline input changed: <file> <item> (now lines a-b) no longer has the recorded hash`.
- **Exactly one node.** `ParsedSource::resolve` reports an invalid selector, an ambiguous selector (a bare selector that does match once `#1` is added), and no matching node as separate errors.
- **Line range.**
  - `ParsedSource::node_range` derives the inclusive range from the outline node, which includes attached comments and attributes. The range is computed at validation time and returned in `ResolvedInput.ranges`.
  - `src/index.rs#fn[render_input]` and `InputLocation::resolve` use those ranges for display.
  - `outline_inputs_for_lines` and `AssessmentSources::read_lines` build outline inputs from line ranges.
- **Missing file.** `read_project_file` and `check_project_file` report a file that cannot be opened or read.
- **Unsupported language.** This case cannot arise in practice, because every non-grammar file falls back to the plain-text profile. The only related failure is a file that cannot be read as UTF-8, which `read_project_file` reports as `cannot read`.

**Tests**
- `tests/evidence_boundaries.rs#fn[outline_inputs_survive_moves_and_unhashed_comments_but_not_edits]` covers most obligations:
  - Moving nodes, reflowing a body, inserting a line before an item and editing a citation comment all leave the inputs valid.
  - Editing code or a doc comment reports "changed hash" with the file, selector and current range. The range for the doc-commented function includes its attached doc and citation comments.
  - An edited plain-text line is no longer found.
  - The error cases are a missing selector, an ambiguous selector, an invalid selector, a missing file and a parse failure (`cannot parse rust source`).
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[collects_missing_orphan_format_false_and_changed_line_errors]` also asserts the changed-hash message on the root node with its range, and the missing-node message.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor]` covers ranges used for coverage.
- `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[fixme_does_not_hide_stale_inputs_or_uncovered_references]` covers the stale-input report.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]` covers the line-range reads and the recorded inputs.
- The remaining `tests/evidence_boundaries.rs` tests cover outline inputs for files outside the repository root: symlinks, configured external paths and generated inputs.

I saw no unspecified observable behavior in the `{impl}` items.

text: :::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
